source.title: Exploring Superposition and Interference in State-of-the-Art Low-Parameter Vision Models
source.authors: Lilian Hollard; Lucas Mohimont; Nathalie Gaveau; Luiz Angelo Steffenel

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses and experimentally studies superposition-related feature interference in low-parameter vision architectures, but does not measure neuron-pole job counts, explanation accuracy, or the interpretability shares named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's own SoLU comparisons and feature-alignment results are recorded as findings about the claim's broader subject, but none measures a named version's outcome. The paper's other cited claims and its ImageNet scaling comparisons are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains low-parameter vision bottleneck networks with and without SoLU and reports accuracy changes and feature-map alignment (Oij). It never measures how many neurons have one job or two, how well neuron explanations predict activations, or interpretable-neuron shares. It does not analyse InceptionV1 neurons, language models or attribution graphs. Its architecture-and-normalization findings concern reliance on feature interference, not the share of interpretable neurons that V4 names, so it tests no version. It also does not cite or use the essay's finding.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that MobileNetv2, MobileNetv3 and MobileNeXt (Batch Norm) rely on interference and scale poorly at very low parameter counts. ConvNeXt, MobileNeXt (Layer Norm), MobileNetv1 and their NoDepth Bottleneck are less affected by SoLU. They argue that reducing reliance on interference improves low-scale scaling, which their NoDepth proof of concept shows on ImageNet.
record.recipe_differences: The study inserts SoLU into vision-model residual streams and compares accuracy and feature-map alignment; it does not use the neuron-pole audit or explanation-testing methods in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with bottleneck architecture and normalization choice: Batch Norm versus Layer Norm.

fits_no_version.finding: SoLU in the residual stream cuts accuracy sharply for Inverted Bottlenecks (about 50%) and MobileNeXt with Batch Norm (42%). The cost is small for ConvNeXt (1–6%) and Layer Norm MobileNeXt/Sandglass (4%). Feature alignment changes under SoLU in the models it hurts and stays stable in the others.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In low-parameter vision CNNs, how much a network relies on feature interference (superposition) depends on bottleneck design and normalization choice.

record.problems: The text gives no uncertainty estimates or control results. Several outcomes are reported qualitatively or as approximate percentages; the Inverted Bottleneck result is aggregated across v2 and v3 rather than separated.
record.rows_left_out: ImageNet scaling and accuracy comparisons for NoDepth Bottleneck are omitted because they do not measure neuron interpretability, job counts, or feature interference. The paper's general accuracy and parameter comparisons for other architectures are likewise outside the claim's named outcomes.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or job counts.
No language models, no mixture-of-experts models, no interpretability shares at scale.
No analysis of InceptionV1 or of the cat-and-car neuron; no test of pose or recursive generalization.
Varies architecture and normalization, but never measures the share of interpretable neurons or the effect of better tools. The 5%–99% estimates are not addressed.
No attribution graphs and no comparison against a replacement model.
No held-out prediction test of explanations drawn from activating examples.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: This is a vision-architecture efficiency paper that uses superposition and SoLU as a lens. It is unrelated to neuron-explanation audits. All rows correctly carry versions none.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit Qwen3-32B or count neuron poles by number of jobs or understanding status.
Does not assess language models, dense versus mixture-of-experts models, or scale to trillions of parameters.
Does not analyze InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron or test the proposed shared-pose explanation or recursive generalization.
Tests architecture-dependent feature interference in vision networks, not the share of interpretable neurons, the effects of explanation tools, or the stated 5%–99% estimates.
Does not build or assess attribution graphs or compare neuron-based analysis with a trained replacement model.
Does not test whether explanations from activating examples predict firing on held-out inputs.
Does not score automated neuron explanations by simulated activations on new text.

rows.subject: Inverted Bottleneck (MobileNetv2 or MobileNetv3)
rows.operation_detail: Compared the base architecture with an implementation using SoLU in the residual stream.
rows.note: The text reports the Inverted Bottleneck result collectively for v2 and v3; it does not give separate model values.

rows.subject: ConvNeXt
rows.operation_detail: Compared the base architecture with its SoLU implementation.
rows.value: interference reduction has no effect; later described as a 1% impact on accuracy
rows.note: The text also reports a separate ConvNeXt configuration with Batch Norm in r3.
rows.check: Subject is incomplete. The Section 4.1 'no effect' statement covers both ConvNeXt and MobileNeXt with Layer Norm (Figure 6), not ConvNeXt alone. The 1% figure comes from Section 4.2.

rows.subject: ConvNeXt
rows.operation_detail: Simulated a standard bottleneck with ReLU and Batch Norm within ConvNeXt and assessed the SoLU comparison.
rows.measure: Average accuracy drop across multiple scaling scenarios
rows.note: Reported as an average across multiple scaling scenarios.

rows.subject: Inverted Bottleneck
rows.operation_detail: Substituted Layer Norm for Batch Norm and compared the SoLU implementation with the base.
rows.note: The paper says Layer Norm alone does not account for ConvNeXt's result.

rows.subject: Sandglass Bottleneck
rows.operation_detail: Compared the Layer Norm Sandglass configuration with and without SoLU.
rows.note: The text reports this experiment as showing a 4% accuracy loss.
rows.check: Sandglass Bottleneck is MobileNeXt's block, so this 4% Layer Norm loss likely duplicates r7's 4% MobileNeXt Layer Norm drop. Keep one row or mark the two as the same result.

rows.subject: MobileNeXt
rows.operation_detail: Compared the Batch Norm model with its SoLU implementation.
rows.note: The paper also describes this as an accuracy drop as severe as 42%.

rows.subject: MobileNeXt
rows.operation_detail: Compared feature organization in the base model and the SoLU model.
rows.note: The text contrasts this with the 42% drop for Batch Norm in r6.
rows.check: operation_detail says feature organization was compared, but the measure is accuracy drop. The feature-organization result is in r11. Probably duplicates r5.

rows.subject: MobileNetv3
rows.operation_detail: Compared channel-axis feature-map directions in the base model and the SoLU-trained model.
rows.baseline: base model: Oij values ranging between 0 and 0.5
rows.value: SoLU-trained model aligns features more closely; no numerical value stated
rows.note: The authors describe the base feature maps as mostly orthogonal and the SoLU model as aligning features more closely.
rows.check: The text attributes a '50% accuracy drop in its baseline form with Batch Norm' to MobileNetv3. This accuracy result is not captured, and Oij values cannot be read beyond the 0–0.5 range stated for the base model.

rows.subject: ConvNeXt
rows.operation_detail: Compared feature-map organization in the base architecture and the SoLU model.
rows.baseline: base architecture: most features organize orthogonally
rows.value: SoLU has no stated significant effect on feature organization; the model follows the same behavior as the base
rows.note: The paper says slight noise or interference naturally aligns within the model's direction space.

rows.subject: MobileNeXt
rows.operation_detail: Examined feature-direction organization and its change under SoLU.
rows.baseline: base model: over 50% of layers exhibit alignment in similar directions
rows.value: SoLU disrupts the architecture's reliance on interference-based representations; no numeric value stated
rows.note: The result is described for the Batch Norm MobileNeXt configuration.

rows.subject: MobileNeXt
rows.operation_detail: Compared feature organization in the base model and the SoLU model.
rows.value: similar high-dimensional organization is maintained; SoLU does not significantly disrupt the structure
rows.note: The authors report this alongside the 4% accuracy drop for Layer Norm MobileNeXt.

rows.subject: NoDepth Bottleneck
rows.operation_detail: Compared feature alignment in the base architecture and the SoLU implementation.

conditions.value: not stated for this feature-alignment comparison

rows.value: alignment remains roughly the same despite interference-noise reduction
rows.note: The text describes the alignment as roughly unchanged, without numerical values.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
